passageTitle: Questions 71-73 refer to the following announcement:
audioScript: Good morning, and thank you for standing in the rain with us. In a few minutes we will cut the ribbon on our newest branch on Camden Street, our 4th location in the county. The store opens to the public at 9 a.m., and the first 50 customers will receive a $20 gift card at the door. Because our parking lot is small, a free shuttle runs every 15 minutes from the Eastside garage until 6 p.m. Inside you will find our full line of gardening supplies, plus a section of outdoor furniture that we are testing here before deciding whether to offer it in other stores. At 11, our head florist leads a free workshop on winter arrangements, and no registration is needed. Anyone spending more than $75 today can also enter a drawing for a small greenhouse.

audioScript: Attention passengers, this is an update on this afternoon's sailings to Brier Island. Because of a mechanical inspection on the ferry Highland Trader, the 2 p.m. crossing has been cancelled and the next departure will be at 4:30. Passengers holding tickets for the 2 p.m. sailing should come to the ticket counter, where staff will either rebook them on the later boat or refund the fare. Vehicles waiting in the loading lane will be moved to the holding area nearby. As the 4:30 boat is filling quickly, we strongly advise arriving 40 minutes before departure. Foot passengers may instead take the shuttle bus to the mainland terminal, which leaves at 3:15 and takes about 90 minutes. We expect the Highland Trader to return to its normal timetable on Thursday morning, and we apologize for the inconvenience.

passageTitle: Questions 77-79 refer to the following announcement:
audioScript: Before we close today's management meeting, here are the highlights of the quarterly safety report. We recorded 14 minor injuries between July and September, down from 23 in the same period last year, and, for the first time in 3 years, no incident that required time off work. Most of the improvement comes from the new guard rails on the loading dock and the glove rule in the paint shop. Two areas still need attention. Forklift speeding in the north aisle accounted for 6 near misses, and emergency exits on level 2 were blocked by pallets on 4 separate inspections. From next month, supervisors will log a 5-minute safety check at the start of every shift, and results will appear on the monthly dashboard. Please remind your teams that reporting a near miss never counts against anyone's record.

passageTitle: Questions 80-82 refer to the following announcement:
audioScript: Welcome to the Cedar Ridge overlook. I am one of the seasonal rangers here and will be with you for about 20 minutes. Before we walk on, 2 reminders. Please stay behind the rope barrier; the rock face beyond it crumbles after heavy rain, and last spring a visitor broke an ankle only a few meters from where you are standing. Also keep food in your packs. The chipmunks here are bold enough to take a sandwich from your hand, and feeding them makes them dependent on visitors. What you see below is a glacial valley carved about 10,000 years ago and drained by a river that changes course almost every decade. The wooden platform we are standing on was rebuilt 2 summers ago with money raised by local schoolchildren. I give this talk again at noon.

audioScript: Hello, and thanks for your interest in our online course, Data Skills for Managers. I am Dr. Ellis, your instructor for the 8-week program. The course is built for people who work with spreadsheets every day but have never written a line of code. Each week you watch 4 short video lessons, complete one practical exercise using a real sales dataset, and join a live discussion on Thursday evenings. Live sessions are recorded, so you will not fall behind if you miss one. You need no special software; everything runs in your browser, and the only extra cost is a $20 certificate fee, which is optional. Students who submit all 8 exercises receive feedback from teaching assistants within 3 working days. The next group starts on March 4, and enrollment closes 1 week before that date.

audioScript: Thank you all for coming out on a Friday evening. Two years ago this community raised $11,000 to rebuild the roof of the River Street shelter, and tonight we hope to beat that figure for a different reason: the shelter now needs a second van to collect donated food from supermarkets before it spoils. Our treasurer, Mr. Okafor, is at the back if you would like to make a pledge.

audioScript: Good afternoon, and welcome to the material testing laboratory. My name is Priya Raman and I will be showing you around for the next 40 minutes. Before we go through those double doors, everyone needs a lab coat and safety glasses, which are in the cabinet by the entrance. Please leave bags on the shelves instead of carrying them, because loose straps catch on equipment. We begin in the tensile testing room, where steel samples are pulled apart to measure their strength, then move to the climate chamber, which simulates temperatures from minus 40 to plus 90 degrees. Photography is allowed everywhere except the room where we handle composite dust, since a flash can disturb a sensitive sensor. We finish in the conference room, where 2 of our engineers will take questions about careers in testing.

audioScript: Residents of Ward 4, this is a reminder about the recycling changes that begin on the first of next month. Glass will no longer go in the blue bin; instead, take bottles and jars to one of the 3 collection points listed on the city website, the nearest being behind the public library. The blue bins themselves are being replaced with larger carts, delivered to your address over the next 3 weeks; until yours arrives, keep using the old bin. Yard waste collection moves from weekly to every other Tuesday, which should cut fuel costs by about 18 percent and allow us to hire 2 extra drivers for the winter routes. Cardboard must be flattened and placed beside the cart, not inside it, because the new trucks sort material by shape. Questions can go to the waste office.

passageTitle: Questions 95-97 refer to the following announcement:
audioScript: Residents of Ward 4, this is a reminder about the recycling changes that begin on the first of next month. Glass will no longer go in the blue bin; instead, take bottles and jars to one of the 3 collection points listed on the city website, the nearest being behind the public library. The blue bins themselves are being replaced with larger carts, delivered to your address over the next 3 weeks; until yours arrives, keep using the old bin. Yard waste collection moves from weekly to every other Tuesday, which should cut fuel costs by about 18 percent and allow us to hire 2 extra drivers for the winter routes. Cardboard must be flattened and placed beside the cart, not inside it, because the new trucks sort material by shape. Questions can go to the waste office.

audioScript: Frequent flyers, this message explains the updates to our Horizon Miles program, effective October 1. Members will now earn miles based on the price of the ticket rather than the distance flown, at a rate of 5 miles per dollar. For most travellers on our short domestic routes this works out slightly better, while those who book deeply discounted long-haul fares may earn less than before. Miles will no longer expire as long as you take at least 1 flight every 2 years, a change members have requested for a long time. Silver status now requires 15 qualifying flights instead of 20, and Silver members get priority boarding on every flight, not only international ones. Reward seats on weekend flights cost 20 percent more miles in July and August. Your current balance is unaffected.
